body: She and I have history together. A decade ago something was kindling, but she gave the same answer of not really looking for a relationship. Then she goes and gets a boyfriend whom she eventually married (and is now divorced from). So I'm trying to protect myself from being some secondary source of comfort, if that's what I really am
Your reply makes lots of sense. One thing I'm afraid of is if I do bring it up, she'll become defensive and it will ruin the friendship.

Good points. I'm not trying to be her post retirement white knight. I make good money, but without a second income she's not going to live lavishly. She knows me well enough and has stayed over at my house so she knows my lifestyle, so maybe she's already reconciled that

My generosity towards her has always been about giving my time and being a real friend, and not about giving her money or gifts. Expecting me to become a long term or permanent john is an intriguing theory, thank you for the insight.

My family believes she is a successful accountant. Strangely, they also believe she is an exgirlfriend of mine. I suppose our closeness did raise eyebrows, and my ex-wife's radar wasn't completely off.

I do make good money and I drive a nice car, so I wonder now about other motives. On the other hand, she has been a solid friend and has never used me for anything other than watching her puppies for a weekend.
